How long does an analysis take in chromosomix, and how much memory does it need, when it is run over a
whole genome on an ordinary laptop? This notebook answers that for 23 analyses on public data: Hi-C maps
from 69 million to 1.08 billion contacts, a yeast Micro-C map down to 50 bp, and ATAC-seq tracks and
sequence over the whole mouse genome.

Each analysis is run once through `chromosomix`, the command-line form of the app's Analysis panel. It
runs the same code the browser runs, and as a separate process its time and memory can be measured by
the operating system: the wall-clock time from start to finish, the CPU time, and the peak memory (the
largest resident set the process reached).

To render it, from the root of a clone, on a laptop that is plugged in and otherwise idle:

```bash
npm ci && npm run build:cli
pip install jupyter pandas matplotlib pyfaidx
quarto render notebooks/laptop.qmd
```

The data (about 13.7 GB) are downloaded once into `notebooks/work/laptop/data/`; files that
`validation.qmd` has already downloaded are linked rather than downloaded again. The analyses take about
45 minutes, most of it peak calling. Each result is saved to `notebooks/work/laptop/timings.tsv` as soon
as it is measured, so a second render reads the table instead of running everything again; set `REDO`
below to start over.

```{python}
import hashlib
import os
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import pyfaidx

REDO = False

HERE = Path.cwd().resolve()
REPO = HERE.parent if HERE.name == 'notebooks' else HERE
CLI = REPO / 'dist-cli' / 'chromosomix.mjs'
WORK = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'laptop'
DATA = WORK / 'data'
TIMINGS = WORK / 'timings.tsv'
DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

if not CLI.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f'{CLI} is not there: run `npm run build:cli` first.')
VERSION = subprocess.run(['node', str(CLI), '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')[0]
```

## The machine

```{python}
def processor():
    if sys.platform == 'darwin':
        return subprocess.run(['sysctl', '-n', 'machdep.cpu.brand_string'], capture_output=True,
                              text=True).stdout.strip()
    if Path('/proc/cpuinfo').exists():
        for line in open('/proc/cpuinfo'):
            if line.startswith('model name'):
                return line.split(':', 1)[1].strip()
    return platform.processor()


MACHINE = {
    'processor': processor(),
    'cores': os.cpu_count(),
    'memory': f"{os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') * os.sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES') / 2**30:.0f} GB",
    'system': platform.platform(),
    'node': subprocess.run(['node', '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(),
    'chromosomix': VERSION.removeprefix('chromosomix '),
}
pd.DataFrame(MACHINE.items(), columns=['', 'this machine']).style.hide(axis='index')
```

## The data

| Data | Source | Contacts | Size |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Mouse Hi-C, mm10 | 4DN 4DNFIOZ1TRUS | 69 million | 0.7 GB |
| Human Hi-C, IMR-90, GRCh38 (Rao et al. 2014) | 4DN 4DNFIJTOIGOI | 1.08 billion | 8.3 GB |
| Yeast Micro-C (Costantino et al. 2020) | GEO GSE151553 | 51 million | 0.1 GB |
| Mouse ATAC-seq, two replicates | 4DN 4DNFIIY4QW2D, 4DNFITBRHVZE | | 1.7 GB |
| Mouse genome sequence and RefSeq genes, mm10 | UCSC, as Illumina iGenomes distributes them | | 2.9 GB |

Every file is checked against its MD5 when it is downloaded. The mouse sequence is indexed beside itself
(`mm10.fa.fai`) so that it is read by range.

```{python}
FOURDN = 'https://4dn-open-data-public.s3.amazonaws.com/fourfront-webprod/wfoutput'
IGENOMES = 'https://ngi-igenomes.s3.amazonaws.com/igenomes/Mus_musculus/UCSC/mm10'
GEO = 'https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series'
FILES = {
    '4DNFIOZ1TRUS.mcool': (f'{FOURDN}/727b405d-c9f5-4b13-ae58-1dbf29d19a8f/4DNFIOZ1TRUS.mcool',
                           '503fea3d171e9c5c7f8a5403af73481e'),
    '4DNFIJTOIGOI.mcool': (f'{FOURDN}/b4939d95-4121-4f86-9cc8-29a34eb834ef/4DNFIJTOIGOI.mcool',
                           '659f9dc7613650494aa5ed4138e2e17e'),
    'GSE151553_A364_merged.mcool': (f'{GEO}/GSE151nnn/GSE151553/suppl/GSE151553_A364_merged.mcool',
                                    '319a04a8d7e41d9eb88e2378ea3ea373'),
    '4DNFIIY4QW2D.bw': (f'{FOURDN}/7fb6d419-a8de-4bc8-9c17-f68f814496a2/4DNFIIY4QW2D.bw',
                        '9f8a3a413f54129a689548a93584cdf4'),
    '4DNFITBRHVZE.bw': (f'{FOURDN}/e567a80e-c7d2-41ff-b12d-67047906c076/4DNFITBRHVZE.bw',
                        '99c928ea99ee1a2a7ec7091260f1e4be'),
    'mm10.fa': (f'{IGENOMES}/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa', '34d90c586dc92f5c3e8df3ed24530f4f'),
    'mm10.genes.gtf': (f'{IGENOMES}/Annotation/Genes/genes.gtf', '543ec24bb11a4ff0cf5aa4f695320b82'),
}
VALIDATION_DATA = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'validation' / 'data'


def md5(path):
    digest = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 22), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def fetch(name, url, expected):
    path = DATA / name
    if path.exists():
        return
    if (VALIDATION_DATA / name).exists():
        path.symlink_to(VALIDATION_DATA / name)
        return
    print('downloading', url)
    part = path.with_name(name + '.part')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, open(part, 'wb') as out:
        shutil.copyfileobj(response, out, 1 << 22)
    if md5(part) != expected:
        part.unlink()
        raise ValueError(f'{url} did not download as published: its MD5 is not {expected}.')
    part.rename(path)


for name, (url, expected) in FILES.items():
    fetch(name, url, expected)
pyfaidx.Faidx(str(DATA / 'mm10.fa')).close()

pd.DataFrame([{'file': name, 'GB': round((DATA / name).stat().st_size / 1e9, 2)} for name in FILES]) \
    .style.hide(axis='index').format(precision=2)
```

## The analyses

Each analysis is one command, run from `notebooks/work/laptop/` with its output in `out/<name>/`. Two of
them read another's output: the pileup (APA) is over the loops chromosight called, and the overlap is
of the peaks called on the ATAC-seq replicates against the RefSeq transcripts. Parameters are the app's
defaults, except where the validation notebook uses others for the same analysis.

```{python}
MOUSE, HUMAN, YEAST = 'data/4DNFIOZ1TRUS.mcool', 'data/4DNFIJTOIGOI.mcool', 'data/GSE151553_A364_merged.mcool'
ATAC1, ATAC2, MM10, GENES = 'data/4DNFIIY4QW2D.bw', 'data/4DNFITBRHVZE.bw', 'data/mm10.fa', 'data/mm10.genes.gtf'
```

Each command runs as a process of its own, and `os.wait4` returns what the system counted of it:
its CPU time, user and system, and its peak resident memory (`ru_maxrss`, which macOS gives in bytes and
Linux in kilobytes).

```{python}
def run(name, args):
    """One command: its wall-clock and CPU seconds, and its peak memory in MB."""
    out = WORK / 'out' / name
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as err:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        process = subprocess.Popen(['node', str(CLI), *args, '--out', f'out/{name}', '--quiet'], cwd=WORK,
                                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        _, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, 0)
        wall = time.perf_counter() - start
        if os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status):
            err.seek(0)
            raise RuntimeError(f'chromosomix {" ".join(args)} failed:\n{err.read().decode()[-3000:]}')
    peak = usage.ru_maxrss / (2**20 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 2**10)
    return {'wall_s': wall, 'cpu_s': usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime, 'peak_mb': peak}


# Results from an earlier render of this same build are kept; the others are run, and saved one by one.
done = pd.read_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t') if TIMINGS.exists() and not REDO else pd.DataFrame()
if len(done):
    done = done[done['chromosomix'] == MACHINE['chromosomix']]
rows = done.to_dict('records')
for name, data, analysis, resolution, args in TASKS:
    if any(row['name'] == name for row in rows):
        continue
    print(f'{name} …', end=' ', flush=True)
    cost = run(name, args)
    print(f"{cost['wall_s']:.1f} s, {cost['peak_mb']:.0f} MB")
    rows.append({'name': name, 'data': data, 'analysis': analysis, 'resolution': resolution, **cost,
                 'command': 'chromosomix ' + ' '.join(args), **MACHINE})
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', index=False)
times = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('name').loc[[task[0] for task in TASKS]].reset_index()
```

## Results

```{python}
def duration(seconds):
    return f'{seconds:.1f} s' if seconds < 60 else f'{seconds / 60:.1f} min'


table = times.assign(time=times['wall_s'].map(duration), cpu=times['cpu_s'].map(duration),
                     memory=times['peak_mb'].round().astype(int))
table[['data', 'analysis', 'resolution', 'time', 'cpu', 'memory']] \
    .rename(columns={'time': 'wall-clock time', 'cpu': 'CPU time', 'memory': 'peak memory (MB)'}) \
    .style.hide(axis='index').format({'peak memory (MB)': '{:,}'})
```

```{python}
slowest = times.loc[times['wall_s'].idxmax()]
largest = times.loc[times['peak_mb'].idxmax()]
under_a_minute = int((times['wall_s'] < 60).sum())
```

On this machine:

- **Under a minute:** `{python} under_a_minute` of the `{python} len(times)` analyses.
- **Slowest:** `{python} slowest['analysis']` (`{python} slowest['data']`), in
  `{python} duration(slowest['wall_s'])`.
- **Most memory:** `{python} f"{largest['peak_mb']:,.0f}"` MB, for `{python} largest['analysis']`
  (`{python} largest['data']`).

The CPU time is close to the wall-clock time because chromosomix computes on one thread; it can be
slightly higher, as Node collects garbage and compiles on threads of its own.

The two Hi-C maps differ 16-fold in depth, on genomes of about the same size. The same five analyses on
each:

```{python}
pairs = []
for name in ['coverage', 'expected', 'insulation', 'compartments', 'loops']:
    mouse = times.set_index('name').loc[name]
    human = times.set_index('name').loc[f'human-{name}']
    pairs.append({'analysis': mouse['analysis'], 'resolution': mouse['resolution'],
                  '69 M contacts': duration(mouse['wall_s']), '1.08 B contacts': duration(human['wall_s']),
                  '69 M, MB': round(mouse['peak_mb']), '1.08 B, MB': round(human['peak_mb'])})
pd.DataFrame(pairs).style.hide(axis='index')
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-laptop
#| fig-cap: "Wall-clock time (left, logarithmic) and peak memory (right) of each analysis, coloured by its data."
colours = dict(zip(times['data'].unique(), ['#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#4f9d69', '#8c6bb1']))
labels = [f'{a} ({r})' for a, r in zip(times['analysis'], times['resolution'])]
y = range(len(times))[::-1]
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 0.3 * len(times) + 1), sharey=True, layout='constrained')
left.barh(y, times['wall_s'], color=times['data'].map(colours))
left.set(xscale='log', xlabel='wall-clock time (s)', yticks=list(y), yticklabels=labels)
right.barh(y, times['peak_mb'], color=times['data'].map(colours))
right.set(xlabel='peak memory (MB)')
for data, colour in colours.items():
    right.barh([], [], color=colour, label=data)
right.legend(loc='lower right', frameon=False, fontsize=8)
for ax in (left, right):
    ax.spines[['top', 'right']].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=8)
plt.show()
```
